claim_text: Rakuten Securities says a third party gained unauthorized access to some of its systems, detected on Nov 16, 2026
summary: The company's Nov 17 notice (Japanese) says it detected a possible unauthorized access by a third party to some of its systems on Nov 16, blocked access to the affected part and made fixes.
detail: The notice says the company's investigation into the cause and the detailed course of events is continuing. The Japan Times and Infosecurity Magazine report the same statements.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: A Tier 1 source, Rakuten Securities' own press release, states the unauthorized access, and two outlets report the same statements.

claim_text: Rakuten Securities says information held in its test environment may have been leaked to an outside party on Nov 11
summary: The notice says its investigation found that on Wed, Nov 11, some information managed inside its test environment system may have leaked outside the company.
detail: The company words this as a possible leak (a risk of leakage), not a confirmed copy. It says it has finished identifying the affected customers and will tell them individually. This is the company's account; no outside party has checked it.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: The company's own notice (Tier 1) says this, and two outlets report it; the label records that the company says it, not that an outsider verified the timing.

claim_text: Rakuten Securities says up to about 4.47 million accounts had personal and financial details exposed
summary: For up to about 4.47 million accounts, the notice lists names, birth dates, addresses, phone numbers, emails, employers, withdrawal bank accounts and self-reported income and assets.
detail: The full list also has branch and customer code, login ID, name in kana, assets by product and last login date (closed accounts included). This is the company's own list of data that may have been taken. The login ID is the brokerage login, not the wider Rakuten ID. Outlets repeat the figures.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Tier 1 company notice gives the categories and the maximum count; two outlets repeat them.

claim_text: Rakuten Securities says up to about 11.25 million further accounts had only a branch and customer code and a login ID exposed
summary: The notice says up to about 11.25 million accounts had their branch and customer code and login ID potentially exposed. It notes this login ID is different from the Rakuten ID.
detail: The two groups are described separately. Press (BreachNews, Yomiuri, Nippon TV) add them to a total of up to about 15.72 million accounts; the notice itself lists the two figures. A company spokesperson reportedly told media the groups do not overlap (BreachNews, one outlet; not independently checked).
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Tier 1 company notice gives the maximum count and fields; outlets repeat them.

claim_text: Rakuten Securities says it has not confirmed any leak of passwords, trading PINs or other information needed to trade, and has found no related unauthorized logins or trades
summary: The notice says leaks of the login password, PIN and other information needed to trade have not been confirmed, and that as of Nov 17 no unauthorized access or trades attributable to this incident had been identified.
detail: This is the company's own statement of what it has not found, made while its investigation is continuing, with the words 'at this time'. No outside check exists. Infosecurity Magazine notes the company said there was no sign of unauthorized access to customer accounts.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: The company's own notice (Tier 1) says it; the label records the company's account only, not an independent finding that nothing was taken.
notes: Label reflects the statement, not proof of absence.

claim_text: Rakuten Securities warns customers of follow-up phishing and says its emails carry no links and it will not phone to ask for personal or login details
summary: The notice urges caution about suspicious email, SMS, calls or mail posing as the company, says the company's emails contain no URLs, and says it will not call to ask for personal or login information.
detail: It also says over 90 percent of daily logins already use passkeys and asks others to set one up, and says customers can switch off trading or withdrawals themselves in the security settings.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: The company's own notice (Tier 1) says this; the Japan Times reports the passkey and suspension advice.

claim_text: The company reportedly said that real customer data had been copied, unmasked, to the test environment during a system upgrade
summary: ITmedia NEWS reports the company told it that part of its real customer data was copied to a test server for a set period during an upgrade without being masked; BreachNews reports the same.
detail: ITmedia NEWS (Nov 18) says the company answered its questions directly: data was copied from production to a test server to check some functions of an internal system upgrade, it was not masked, the step went through formal internal approval and was not one employee's decision, and the company normally keeps only dummy data in test systems. The company declined to say when the data was moved or how long the upgrade work ran. BreachNews (Tier 3) reports the same comments and likely relies on the same reporting, so the two count as one source. Tokyo Shimbun (Nov 21) and TV Asahi (Nov 20) instead report the company says whether the data was masked is still under investigation. Because the accounts conflict and the company's own notices do not address masking, this stays Reported.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: One Tier 2 outlet (ITmedia NEWS) quotes the company directly; BreachNews appears to relay the same comments. Later Tokyo Shimbun and TV Asahi reports conflict, and the company's own notices do not say it.
notes: Re-label Confirmed only on the company's own page or another independent outlet with its own company comment, and only if the conflict with Tokyo Shimbun's report is resolved. Real data in the test environment is c013; this claim is only about the data being unmasked.

claim_text: Rakuten Securities says Japan's Financial Services Agency ordered it on Nov 19 to report on the incident
summary: The company's Nov 19 release says it received an order on Nov 19 under Article 56-2(1) of the Financial Instruments and Exchange Act and Article 146(1) of the Personal Information Protection Act to report on the incident.
detail: Yomiuri and Nippon TV report the order; Nippon TV says the financial services minister confirmed it and called it very regrettable, saying the agency would verify the report and respond strictly. Yomiuri says the agency judged the order necessary because of the scale and sensitivity of the data. NHK, Sankei and Tokyo Shimbun also report the order and the minister's comments. ITmedia NEWS (Nov 20) reports the minister said the agency is working closely with the police and Japan's National Cybersecurity Office, and has asked the company to check any reported fraudulent trade at once and report it to the agency; the Finance Ministry's own published summary of the Nov 20 press conference records these remarks, adds that the minister was told no fraudulent trades have been found so far, and says the agency will also check how the company stored customer data. We did not find a Financial Services Agency page on the order itself.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: A Tier 1 company release says it received the order, the Finance Ministry's published press-conference summary records the minister confirming it, and several Japanese outlets report it independently.

claim_text: How the attacker got in, and what flaw or method was used
summary: The company says the cause and detailed course of events are still under investigation.
detail: ITmedia NEWS reports the company told it that it had security measures in place but an attacker exploited a vulnerability; BreachNews reports the same. Neither names the vulnerability, and the company's own notices do not mention it. No forensic report has been published. A published root cause is needed before this story can close.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: The company itself says the cause is still being investigated.

claim_text: Who carried out the unauthorized access
summary: No source names an attacker, group or country.
detail: We found no attribution by the company, a government body or an independent analyst. We did not visit any leak site, dark-web page or tracker.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: No source in our set names an actor.

claim_text: Whether any ransom demand or data publication has been claimed
summary: We found no outlet reporting a ransom demand, extortion claim or publication of the data.
detail: We looked only at news coverage and company pages, and did not visit leak sites, dark-web pages or trackers. Absence from the coverage we read is not proof that none exists.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: None of the outlets we read reports such a claim.

claim_text: Whether this breach is linked to Rakuten Group's earlier incidents or to other recent attacks on Japanese securities firms
summary: The Japan Times notes that Rakuten Travel and Rakuten Drive disclosed separate incidents last month and that other Japanese securities firms reported leaks, but it does not link them to this one.
detail: We found no official or independent source tying this breach to any of those incidents. They are listed as context only.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: The Japan Times describes them as separate disclosures and does not connect them.

claim_text: Rakuten Securities says it used real customer data in its test environment to check a system update
summary: Japanese and English outlets report that the company used actual customer information, not the dummy data it normally uses, in the test environment the data may have leaked from.
detail: Tokyo Shimbun reports the company's press office said real data was needed to check a system update and that the use was approved internally; it also reports the company says whether the data was masked is still under investigation. ITmedia NEWS reports the company told it real data was needed to check some functions of an internal system upgrade and that it normally keeps only dummy data in test systems. The Japan Times, running a Jiji report, says the company normally uses dummy data in testing but actual customer information was included this time. The company's own notices do not mention it. This is the company's account as relayed by the press.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Three independent Tier 2 outlets (Tokyo Shimbun, Jiji, ITmedia NEWS) report it from the company; BreachNews (Tier 3) says the same.
notes: Whether the data was masked is not established (see c007).

claim_text: A Tokyo law firm is gathering customers for a possible class action against Rakuten Securities
summary: The Japan Times reports at least 15,000 people had registered interest by Nov 20, according to a lawyer for the claimants.
detail: The firm says it will decide whether to file depending on how many people sign up and what the company does next. No lawsuit had been filed as of that report. The Japan Times also reports the company had not said whether it will compensate customers.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: One Tier 2 outlet, citing the law firm organizing claimants.
